item.title: Iterated Lavrentiev regularization under random noise: variational source conditions and rates in expectation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The convergence theory of iterated Lavrentiev regularization for nonlinear monotone ill-posed equations is deterministic: the data error is bounded by a known level that the discrepancy principle uses explicitly. Under Gaussian noise no such bound exists. For a discretized two-dimensional nonlinear inverse source problem for the Poisson equation, we analyse convergence in a finite-energy Gaussian noise model, keeping the linearized and nonlinear cases apart. For the linearized iteration the noisy and noise-free iterates differ by one resolvent applied to the noise; this gives an exact singular-value variance formula, a priori rates in expectation, and the main result: for a family of discretizations whose distance functions are bounded uniformly in the mesh, the rate is governed by that decay, which relaxes the classical range condition. The rate degrades gracefully, down to logarithmic, as the underlying continuum error loses smoothness, and a balancing rule attains it without knowing the smoothness. For the full nonlinear iteration under the order-one source condition, a truncated discrepancy principle fed only the noise level attains $\sigma_E^{1/2}$ in expectation, in the energy noise level $\sigma_E\asymp\sigma/h$, the rare event of large noise being controlled by concentration. The rough nonlinear regime and the general-exponent nonlinear rate are left open and supported numerically for kink and jump errors. We separate the deterministic worst-case, Gaussian, and white-noise settings, prove a worst-case lower bound, and describe where the method is statistically inefficient relative to spectral cut-off. Heterogeneous media and a cost comparison with an adjoint-based scheme are given as supplementary material.
item.dc:creator: Ankit Singh, Hemant Sharma, Kiran Davuluri

item.title: A noise-level-free parameter-choice rule for iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear potential monotone ill-posed problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.26966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations $F(x)=y$ in a Hilbert space, where $F$ is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fr\'echet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution $x^\dg$ (a locally \emph{potential} operator), and only noisy data $y^\delta$ with unknown noise norm $\delta:=\|y-y^\delta\|$ is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^\delta=x_k^\delta-\bigl(F'(x_k^\delta)+\alpha_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta+\alpha_k(x_k^\delta-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require $\delta$. We analyze a \emph{noise-level-free} parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer $k_*$ of $\theta(k,y^\delta)=\|F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta\|^2/\alpha_k^2$ over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and $\alpha_{k_*}^2\ge c\,\delta/\|x_0-x^\dg\|$. If moreover $x_0-x^\dg\in\R(F'(x^\dg))$ and $k_*\ge1$, we prove $\|x_{k_*}^\delta-x^\dg\|=O(\sqrt{\delta_*}+\sqrt{\delta})$ with the computable $\delta_*=\|F(x_{k_*}^\delta)-y^\delta\|$ satisfying $\kappa\delta\le\delta_*\le C\sqrt\delta$, yielding the baseline rate $O(\delta^{1/4})$ along admissible growing-horizon families, and $O(\sqrt\delta)$ whenever $\delta_*=O(\delta)$; no range-invariance or tangential cone conditions are imposed. Rates under H\"older source conditions with $p\ge1$ (including saturation) follow; the case $p<1$, the removal of the self-adjointness assumption, and a full oracle inequality are identified as open problems.
item.dc:creator: Ankit singh, Hemant Sharma

item.title: Data-driven accelerated multigrid method for Riesz space fractional diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multigrid method is one of the most efficient iterative methods for solving large structured linear systems, and its efficiency stems from the complementarity between the smoother and the coarse grid correction. In this paper, we consider the block Toeplitz linear system obtained by discretizing time dependent Riesz space fractional diffusion equations, and employ the weighted Jacobi iterative method as a smoother. The weighted Jacobi smoother features a simple structure and low computational cost, yet its smoothing property is highly dependent on the relaxation parameter. We adopt Gaussian process regression to select the relaxation parameter to accelerate the convergence of the multigrid method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical analysis, which simultaneously verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the data-driven parameter selection strategy.
item.dc:creator: Yang Hu, Juan Zhang

item.title: Structure-Preserving Numerical Schemes for a Time-Fractional Porous Medium Equation with Nonlocal Pressure

item.title: Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Pablo Tejerina-P\'erez, Leonid Sarieddine, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez, Marisol Traforetti, Pau Sol\'e-Vilar\'o, Oleksii Ignatenko, Nazar Tkach, Pavlos Protopapas

item.title: Convolution Quadrature with Adaptive History Compression for Variable-Order Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a fully implicit fast method for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction--diffusion equations with periodic fractional diffusion and exponential-transition Scarpi memory. A Volterra-resolvent analysis establishes local well-posedness and temporal regularity estimates that describe the weak initial singularity. Backward Euler convolution quadrature combined with Fourier pseudospectral discretization achieves mesh-uniform stability and positive-time first-order convergence. To accelerate the scheme, we utilize Cauchy--FFT weight recovery and adaptive blockwise sum-of-exponentials compression, which significantly reduces the cost of history evaluation under local error control. A logarithmic perturbation bound quantifies the effects of weight recovery, history compression, and inexact nonlinear solves, giving tolerance conditions that preserve the convergence order. Numerical experiments confirm the first-order accuracy and demonstrate that the accelerated method efficiently resolves long-time spatial patterns at a substantially reduced computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Pu Yuan, Paul Zegeling

item.title: Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.27500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-\gamma Q^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, \gamma >0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schr\"odinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.
item.dc:creator: Chandler Haight, Alex D Rodriguez, Svetlana Roudenko

item.title: Trace Inverse Estimates and Kernel-based Nitsche Galerkin Methods for Elliptic Interface Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish trace inverse estimates for products of independently generated Sobolev-kernel trial spaces on Lipschitz subdomains and use them to analyze symmetric Nitsche Galerkin methods for elliptic interface problems. The estimates control one-sided gradient traces by subdomain gradients, the interface jump, and an exterior boundary trace. Their conormal form provides the flux control required by the Nitsche formulation without imposing value constraints on the trial spaces, including configurations with an interior inclusion. For quasi-uniform center families with comparable fill distances and a fixed kernel scale, we obtain coercivity and well-posedness for sufficiently large penalty parameters independent of refinement. We prove energy and $L^2$ error bounds of orders $h^{s-1}$ and $h^s$ for piecewise $H^s$ solutions, $2\le s\le m$, where $h$ is the maximum fill distance and $m$ is the kernel Sobolev order. The $L^2$ bound additionally requires piecewise $H^2$ regularity of the homogeneous adjoint interface problem. For scaled kernels $\Phi_{m,\varepsilon}$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$, we also derive a scale-explicit condition-number bound in the kernel-translate basis. The analysis assumes exact geometry and integration. Planar experiments examine convergence and support scaling, whereas a three-dimensional mixed-boundary calculation illustrates the method.
item.dc:creator: Leevan Ling, Shu Ma, Weifeng Qiu, Yizhong Sun

item.title: Multi-time-stepping splitting scheme with mass lumping for the multiscale wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.27715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient simulation of wave propagation in high-contrast media is challenging because standard explicit schemes are subject to severe time-step restrictions induced by fine spatial scales and fast multiscale modes, whereas fully implicit schemes require costly globally coupled solves. In this work, we develop a mass-lumped multi-time-stepping partially explicit splitting method for multiscale wave equations. Based on a nonlocal multicontinuum (NLMC) decomposition of the approximation space, the solution is separated into contrast-dependent fast components and contrast-independent slow components, which are advanced implicitly and explicitly, respectively. A mass-lumping approximation diagonalizes the coarse-scale mass operator and removes the coupling between two subproblems, thus enabling multirate time integration for the two parts. To further improve efficiency, we introduce a residual-based adaptive strategy that dynamically adjusts the time step of the explicitly treated subsystem according to its temporal error indicator. The proposed scheme is shown to be energy stable under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed mass-lumped multi-time-stepping scheme substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy comparable to that of standard fully implicit methods.
item.dc:creator: Yating Wang, Wing Tat Leung, Zhengya Yang, Shufan Li

item.title: The Dimension Landscape of Bivariate $C^2$ Splines
item.description: arXiv:2610.27814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schumaker's lower bound incorporates local geometric corrections and provides insight into the dimensions of bivariate spline spaces. Building on this bound, we study bivariate $C^2$ spline dimensions from three perspectives: universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps. We prove universal attainment in degree seven for every legal realization of every triangulation. We prove generic attainment in degrees five and six for every fixed combinatorial triangulation and give explicit polynomial conditions certifying generic failure on fixed triangulations in degrees three and four. For geometric jumps with matching local direction types at corresponding interior vertices, we prove nonexistence in degree seven and construct examples in degrees three and five. In degree six, universal attainment and the existence of such geometric jumps remain open questions.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Wu, Jiansong Deng

item.title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. However, the method usually leads to ill-conditioned linear systems with a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), limiting its application. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.
item.dc:creator: Likun Qiu, Jianguo Huang, Xuejun Xu

item.title: Front-pinned spectral collocation for the flame problem and related ignition problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider global Chebyshev collocation for the ignition problems $y'=y^q(1-y)$, $y(0)=\delta$, $q\ge2$; for $q=2$ this is the flame problem, a standard stiff test equation. After rescaling to $[-1,1]$ the solution has an interior layer of width $O(\mu)$, $\mu=(q-1)\delta^{q-1}$, at a $\delta$-dependent position. Two obstacles arise: plain Chebyshev collocation needs $O(1/\mu)$ nodes, and imposing the initial condition amplifies errors by a factor of order $1/\mu$, which makes the collocation equations severely ill-conditioned. Our main contribution addresses the second one. Since all solutions are translates of one profile, the initial condition can be replaced by an equivalent interior condition. For an unknown $u=\varphi(y)$, imposing it where the speed $|\varphi'f_q|$ of $u$ along the orbit is maximal bounds the propagator of the linearized equation by one; for $u=\ln y$ this is $y(x^\ast)=(q-1)/q$. For the first obstacle we use the sinh map of Tee and Trefethen: the time function is explicit, the complex singularities of the profile lie exactly at $\pm(2k+1)\pi i$, and the map parameters follow in closed form, so that $O(\ln(1/\mu))$ nodes suffice. In double precision the pinned scheme reaches the interpolation error of the exact solution in five or six Newton iterations for $\mu$ down to $10^{-12}$, whereas the initial-condition form fails or converges to wrong discrete solutions, also in an integral (Birkhoff) reformulation. Computations in $256$-bit arithmetic confirm the predicted rate down to errors of $10^{-70}$, AAA approximation locates the singularities to within $2\%$, and the method carries over to an Arrhenius reaction rate, with all parameters computed numerically.
item.dc:creator: Imre Boros

item.title: Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.27869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the following inverse domain uncertainty quantification problem: given a prescribed value or measurement of a hemodynamic biomarker, characterize the distribution of vascular geometries compatible with it. The problem is formulated as a Bayesian inverse problem in which a high-dimensional latent parameter encodes the cardiovascular shape and accounts for inter-patient variability. The parameter-to-observable map composes a conditional LDDMM stochastic interpolant generating the aortic surface with a high-performance numerical finite element solver for the unsteady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations, from which biomarkers of interest are evaluated. The map is nonlinear, high-dimensional and computationally expensive. To address the problem, we compare three ensemble strategies: ensemble adjusted Kalman inversion (EAKI), adaptive Bayesian updating with structural reliability (aBUS), and a Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) sequential Monte Carlo scheme. The first two approaches are derivative-free. For the third method, we introduce a novel differentiable flow-matching surrogate that reduces the cost of a single forward map evaluation at the price of a distribution shift depending on the training distribution used for the surrogate. We apply the framework to the generation of virtual patient cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops along aortic geometries affected by coarctation, and we validate and compare the three methods on synthetic data.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Romor, Jose Rodrigo Rojo-Garcia, Andr\'e-Alexander Zepernick, Ana Djurdjevac, Alfonso Caiazzo

item.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of model order reduction (MOR) in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). We prove generalizations of well-known necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models, originally stated for rational functions in $H_2$ Hardy-Hilbert spaces. We construct an alternative to the iterative rational Krylov (IRKA) algorithm for RKHSs with differentiable kernels to obtain norm-optimal reduced-order models. Then, we introduce generalized Malmquist-Takenaka (GMT) functions that can be used to define orthonormal bases in an arbitrary RKHS. Using GMT functions, we propose unitary transformations between separable RKHSs. This allows us to extend our optimality conditions and subsequent algorithms to MOR problems posed in RKHSs with non-differentiable kernels. The potential and versatility of the proposed MOR framework is demonstrated in several numerical experiments. We perform norm-optimal MOR on various machine learning models such as support vector machines and deep ReLU networks. In addition, we show how the proposed MOR framework can be used to solve seemingly unrelated problems. In particular, we provide an example for fitting high degree polynomials to data and also obtain a FEM-like method for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with an optimal kernel basis.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Andrea Angino, Rolf Krause, Matthias Voigt

item.title: Density Evolution for Stochastic Dynamical Systems Driven by {\alpha}-Stable Processes: An Equation-Free Numerical Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.28243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While well-established approaches exist for computing probability densities of stochastic differential equations driven by Brownian motion, computing probability densities for general stochastic differential equations driven by {\alpha}-stable processes remains challenging, and few general-purpose methods are available. A major difficulty is that the corresponding Fokker--Planck equations governing the density are generally unavailable in explicit form. In this paper, we develop an efficient approach to compute probability densities for stochastic differential equations driven by {\alpha}-stable processes without relying on Fokker--Planck equations or any other governing equations. The proposed approach is easy to implement and computationally efficient. Numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness and indicate an approximately first-order convergence rate with respect to the time step.
item.dc:creator: Yan Liu, Xu Sun

item.title: First-Order Mean Field Games with Time-Measurable and $C ^{1,1}$ Hamiltonians: Analysis and Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and analyze a numerical framework for a class of first-order, non-local Mean Field Game (MFG) systems with two sources of low regularity: the time-dependent data are merely measurable, and the Hamiltonian is only of class $C^{1,1}$ with respect to the momentum variable. The proposed method combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation with a Lagrange--Galerkin discretization of the continuity equation. Temporal measurability is handled by averaging the data over the time-grid intervals and using the stability theory of $L^1$-viscosity solutions. The limited regularity of the Hamiltonian is addressed through arguments from nonsmooth analysis, based in particular on Clarke's generalized differential calculus. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to some subsequence, to a solution of the MFG system. As a consequence, the numerical approximation also provides a constructive existence result. Under a monotonicity assumption on the coupling terms, we show that the solution to the MFG system is unique, implying the convergence of the whole sequence of discrete solutions. Finally, numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions illustrate the robustness of the method, including a linear--quadratic example with a running cost that is discontinuous in time and for which we compute an exact solution.
item.dc:creator: Elisabetta Carlini, Valentina Coscetti, Francisco J. Silva

item.title: Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.28372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Li, Jiale Meng, Zhenlin Guo, Jiwei Zhang

item.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via M\"uller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nystr\"om discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.
item.dc:creator: Carlos P\'erez-Arancibia, Tao Yin

item.title: Strong Convergence of Fully Discrete Tamed Euler Approximations for Time-Changed Stochastic Delay Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.28552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the strong convergence of a fully discrete equidistant tamed Euler--Maruyama (ETEM) method for time-changed stochastic delay differential equations (TCSDDEs) with state-dependent $\mathrm{d}t$ drifts. A coupled one-sided condition on the subordinator-driven drift and diffusion allows superlinear coefficients with polynomial growth in both the current and delayed states. For subordinators whose Laplace exponent satisfies $\psi(\lambda)\geq c_1\lambda^\alpha$ for all sufficiently large $\lambda$, with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, we derive strong error bounds in terms of the time step $\Delta$ and the subordinator sampling step $\delta$, without imposing a relationship between them. Comparing the partitions generated by the exact and approximate inverse subordinators controls the sampling error without introducing a factor proportional to the number of time steps. For coefficients Lipschitz in both time arguments and Lipschitz history, the scheme achieves a strong convergence rate of order $\Delta^{\alpha/2}(1+|\log\Delta|)^{(1-\alpha)/2}+\sqrt{\delta(1+|\log\delta|)}$. A terminal lower bound $c(\Delta^{\alpha/2}+\delta^{1/2})$ for a multiplicative-noise equation with a stable subordinator establishes the sharpness of both polynomial exponents for this Euler scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate convergence for nonautonomous and multidimensional superlinear delay equations, as well as delay equations with low-regularity time dependence.
item.dc:creator: Ruchun Zuo, Qian Guo

item.title: A Statistical Imaging Framework for Inverse Obstacle Scattering and Its Resolution Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.28553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general statistical framework for inverse obstacle imaging and resolution analysis from far-field second moments under random illumination. The regularized $Q$-statistic is introduced and utilized to measure the minimal statistically weighted cost of synthesizing the test far field associated with a sampling point. Its reciprocal provides an imaging indicator. Under uniform full-aperture plane-wave illumination, we relate this indicator to several classical sampling indicators and derive their statistical counterparts for general random illumination. For the resolution analysis, separating the effects of radiation and noise from the statistics of induced boundary sources, we measure a correlation-free resolution limit by the one-sided half-height width of the boundary transition. In the regime of fixed wavenumber $k$ with the noise-calibrated regularization level $\rho_\tau\to 0$, we establish a sharp asymptotic law for this width for simply connected domains with analytic boundaries. The width scales as \(h_\Gamma(x)\log\log(1/\rho_\tau)/\log(1/\rho_\tau)\), with $h_\Gamma(x)$ a geometric prefactor along the boundary determining both the boundary image contrast and the local transition width. For general boundary-source statistics, we examine how the source mean, variance, and correlation affect imaging quality. Finally, in representative scattering configurations, we provide qualitative interpretations of some typical imaging phenomena through the statistical structure of their induced boundary sources. Numerical examples illustrate these mechanisms and indicate that practical resolution is governed jointly by source statistics, radiation, the noise level, rather than by wavelength alone.
item.dc:creator: Jinrui Zhang, Hai Zhang

item.title: Emulating DGEMM and ZGEMM with INT8 Matrix Engines on Intel Arc GPUs: Ozaki Scheme II on the Xe2 Architecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.26945v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Double-precision matrix multiplication, real (DGEMM) and complex (ZGEMM), dominates the run time of dense linear algebra and electronic-structure codes. On affordable GPUs, however, FP64 throughput is a small and shrinking fraction of the throughput of the low-precision matrix engines. Ozaki scheme II closes this gap by reducing a floating-point matrix product to a handful of exact INT8 products followed by a Chinese-remainder reconstruction; the number of products sets the accuracy. We present what is, to our knowledge, the first implementation of Ozaki scheme II for Intel GPUs. Written in SYCL on top of oneMKL, it runs entirely on the device and exposes the full BLAS dgemm/zgemm interface. Making the scheme fast on the Xe2 (Battlemage) architecture required keeping FP64 arithmetic out of all memory-bound kernels, a branch-free residue computation, an FP32 evaluation of the CRT quotient with a proven safety margin, 16-bit limb arithmetic in the reconstruction, and work-arounds for performance cliffs of the vendor INT8 GEMM. On an Intel Arc Pro B60 (24 GB) the emulated DGEMM reaches 17.3, 12.1 and 9.3 TFLOP/s with $s=8$, 12 and 16 moduli at $N=8192$, and up to 21.1 TFLOP/s overall, i.e. 12-28x the native FP64 DGEMM of the same board. The emulated ZGEMM, which uses the 3M form exactly in integer arithmetic, reaches up to 27.4 TFLOP/s and is 13.7-17.8x faster than native ZGEMM for $N\ge4096$ at $s=16$. With $s\ge16$ the results are correctly rounded for well-scaled inputs and, using an extended-width residue path ($s=20$-24), also for inputs with wide exponent ranges, whereas native DGEMM rounds only 2-13% of the entries correctly. We also report worst-case accuracy, phase breakdowns, energy, an ablation study, a comparison with Ozaki scheme I, and a validated performance model.
item.dc:creator: Rostislavs Rostovskis, Aleksandrs Platonenko

item.title: Beyond exponential tilting: sharp asymptotics and improved importance sampling for rare events
item.description: arXiv:2610.27434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A classical approach for importance sampling (IS) of a rare event is to tilt the measure using its large deviation minimizer, thereby shifting the proposal mean towards the event set. While this tilt is log-efficient, we show that the coefficient of variation of the resulting estimator still grows like $\varepsilon^{-1/4}$ in the small-noise limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Motivated by sharp large deviation asymptotics and the local geometry of the event set at the minimizer, we propose improvements using a control variate or an anisotropic, non-Gaussian proposal. We prove, up to truncations that hold with high probability, and confirm empirically in high-dimensional examples, that the former bounds the coefficient of variation and the latter makes it vanish, so that a bounded number of samples suffices. Our analysis addresses both the coefficient of variation of the different proposals and their necessary and sufficient sample size based on the Kullback--Leibler divergence of the IS target from the proposal; both yield the same rates in $\varepsilon$. We demonstrate the resulting samplers, including a variant that blends the classical and the new proposal across noise levels, for a stochastic Korteweg--de Vries equation with thousands of random inputs.
item.dc:creator: Mingxin Li, Hans Reimann, Timo Schorlepp, Georg Stadler

item.title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.27878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.
item.dc:creator: Fu Zheng, Wei Liu, Xu Qian

item.title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. Numerical optimization involving stiff evolutionary and static PDEs often requires solving a large system of equations, which can be treated as a constraint. In this work, we present a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver that incorporates this constraint. We evaluate its performance across four key tasks: a) linear and nonlinear forward modeling of evolutionary and static problems, b) solving inverse problems to estimate equation coefficients, c) solving inverse problems to estimate the right-hand side, and d) learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. These capabilities make it a powerful tool for different physics and engineering applications, in particular for geophysics, where inverse problems are commonly solved in order to reduce the model uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Yavich, Alexander Ryabov, Viacheslav Naumov, Sayan Ranu, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Evgeny Burnaev, Vladimir Vanovskiy

item.title: Convergence of pivoted Cholesky for Lipschitz kernels
item.description: arXiv:2509.13582v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the continuous analogue of the Cholesky factorization, namely the pivoted Cholesky algorithm. Our analysis establishes quantitative convergence guarantees for kernels of minimal smoothness. We prove that for a symmetric positive definite Lipschitz continuous kernel $K:\Omega\times \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ on a compact domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, the residual of the Cholesky algorithm with complete pivoting (where the maximum value of the diagonal of the residual is selected as the next pivot) is uniformly bounded above by a constant multiple of the separation distance of the pivots, which implies the convergence rate $\|R_n\|_\infty=\mathcal{O}(n^{-1/d})$, where $R_n$ is the residual after $n$ Cholesky steps and $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm. Along the way, we show that for any pivoting strategy, $\|R_n\|_\infty$ is bounded by a constant multiple of the fill distance of the pivots. Moreover, if $K$ is differentiable in both variables with a Lipschitz derivative and $\Omega$ is convex, our convergence rate improves to $\mathcal{O}(n^{-2/d})$. Our result closes a gap between theory and practice as previous analyses required $K$ to be $C^2$-regular or translation invariant to establish convergence, whereas empirical evidence indicated robust performance even for non-differentiable kernels. We further prove a connection between the Cholesky algorithm and the P-greedy interpolation method, as well as downstream applications to Gaussian process regression and matrix Cholesky factorization.
item.dc:creator: Sungwoo Jeong, Alex Townsend, Christopher Wang

item.title: Perturbed saddle-point problems in $\mathrm{L}^p$ with non-regular loads
item.description: arXiv:2603.10532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we develop the continuous and discrete solvability analysis for perturbed saddle-point problems in Banach spaces with forcing terms regularised by means of a projector constructed using the adjoint of a weighted Cl\'ement quasi-interpolation. We take as driving example the linearised Poisson--Boltzmann equation (an advection-diffusion-reaction problem) in mixed form. We use perturbation arguments on the continuous and discrete levels and then derive a priori estimates that remain valid when the load that appears on the right-hand side of the "second" equation is in $\mathrm{H}^{-1}$. Further, we show a supercloseness result and {analyse convergence} of an adequate adaptation of Stenberg postprocessing for mixed advection equations with non-regular data. We provide numerical results that illustrate the convergence of the proposed scheme.
item.dc:creator: Abeer F. Alsohaim, Tomas F\"uhrer, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier, Segundo Villa-Fuentes

item.title: Born-Preconditioned Learning for Iterative Neural PDE Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2603.18527v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Simulating high-frequency waves in spatially varying media remains challenging for both classical iterative methods and neural PDE solvers. We propose Neural Preconditioned Born Series (NPBS), a framework for learning iterative neural PDE solvers. Our guiding idea is to use a simple reference preconditioner to help learn a more effective neural preconditioner. Building on the Convergent Born Series (CBS), NPBS feeds a preconditioned residual to a neural network that predicts a solution update. We train the network to reduce the preconditioned residual after each update. The same reference preconditioner is used for the network input and the loss, giving a metric-matched training objective. Experiments on heterogeneous Helmholtz problems show reduced iteration counts across neural architectures and larger gains at higher wavenumbers. Within a Krylov solver, NPBS achieves the lowest wall-clock time in the evaluated solver comparison. The framework also extends naturally to three-dimensional problems. The same metric-matched formulation also improves convergence on convection-diffusion-reaction systems and Newton linear systems for nonlinear PDEs, indicating that NPBS provides a general framework for learning neural preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Juntao Wang, Jiwei Jia, Xinliang Liu

item.title: Rigorous High-Order Hausdorff Dimension Estimation of Limit Sets of Continued Fraction Iterated Function Systems via B-Splines
item.description: arXiv:2604.20812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a method for the rigorous estimation of Hausdorff dimensions of limit sets produced by continued fraction iterated function systems. Our method is based on the approximation of a Perron-Frobenius operator using the finite element method with B-splines as the choice of basis functions. This choice provides key numerical advantages including higher-order convergence and computational flexibility. We prove an analogue of Falk and Nussbaum's result on ``hidden positivity" for B-spline quasi-interpolants to give rigorous upper and lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimensions of various limit sets. We provide numerical results for degree 4 B-spline interpolants in one and two dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Brown

item.title: Flexible GMRES converges in two phases
item.description: arXiv:2604.27971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the residuals produced by the flexible GMRES (FGMRES) method. The bound shows that FGMRES exhibits two phases of convergence depending on the residual tolerance of the inner preconditioner. For small tolerances, the convergence of FGMRES is practically geometric with a constant rate throughout, while for looser tolerances the two-phase behavior becomes more pronounced. We also show that the derived bound cannot be improved and construct an example for which it becomes an equality.
item.dc:creator: Stefan G\"uttel, Lauri Nyman

item.title: Robust mixed methods for coupled Darcy--Forchheimer--transport problems
item.description: arXiv:2606.14630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We adapt the recent theory for unique solvability of perturbed saddle-point problems in Banach spaces to the case of parameter-independent stability bounds. This also constitutes an extension to the Brezzi--Braess theory for parameter-robust stability of perturbed saddle-point problems from the Hilbert to the Banach setting. We apply the new abstract result to the mixed formulation of the advection-diffusion-reaction equation and tackle also its coupling with the Darcy--Forchheimer equations. The complete system is shown to be stable irrespective of the model parameters of permeability, Forchheimer coefficient, and reaction modulation. We discretise the problem with mixed finite element methods and show convergence in appropriately parameter-weighted norms. We also design operator-based preconditioners for the full system, utilising weighted norms that provide robustness with respect to some model parameters. We also present a few numerical examples that show the convergence and robustness of the proposed method in some regimes of practical interest.
item.dc:creator: Rishi Das, Harsha Hutridurga, Amiya K. Pani, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier

item.title: $H^2(\Omega)$ A Priori Error Bounds for Boundary-Adapted PINNs Solving Elliptic Dirichlet Problems
item.description: arXiv:2607.19167v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the numerical resolution of uniformly elliptic Dirichlet boundary value problems (BVPs) by minimization of the PDE residual over a hypothesis space of Neural Networks made to satisfy exactly the boundary conditions through multiplication by a user-defined \emph{distance-to-boundary approximation} $\rho$. While an $L^2(\partial\Omega)$ boundary penalty cannot generally guarantee $H^2(\Omega)$ error control, we show that exact enforcement can, provided $\rho$ is chosen appropriately. More precisely, we identify a sharp sufficient condition on $\rho$ preserving the regularity needed for $H^2(\Omega)$ error control, provide practical constructions of such $\rho$ for general smooth domains $\Omega$, and refer to the resulting networks as \emph{boundary-adapted}. For boundary-adapted Rectified Quadratic Unit (ReQU) and hyperbolic tangent (tanh) networks, we then derive explicit high-probability $H^2(\Omega)$ convergence rates by combining approximation-theoretic and statistical-learning arguments, making explicit the dependence on $\rho$. Numerical experiments support our theoretical results, showing that appropriate choices of $\rho$ improve accuracy and convergence, while poorly chosen distance functions can substantially degrade the solution. Our proof also yields new VC-dimension bounds for hypothesis spaces of higher-order derivatives of ReQU and tanh networks, together with new approximation bounds for shallow ReQU networks in higher-order Sobolev norms, all of which are of important independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Nathanael Tepakbong, Jun Fan, Xiang Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou

item.title: Scaled boundary cubature scheme in higher dimensions: integration over polytopes and curved regions
item.description: arXiv:2608.15563v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the scaled boundary cubature (SBC) scheme from planar regions to higher-dimensional regions described by oriented boundary patches. The resulting parametrization transforms integrals over compact regions in $\mathbb{R}^d$ into sums of integrals over the boundary-patch parameter domains and a radial coordinate. In three dimensions, this yields a direct volume-integration rule for solids bounded by affine faces, triangular or tensor-product surface patches, B-spline patches, NURBS patches, and combinations of curved and affine boundary representations. For affine polytopes, recursive application of the scaled boundary map yields nested tensor-product rules over simplex sectors; in three dimensions, these reduce to tetrahedral-sector rules that apply equally to convex and nonconvex oriented polyhedra. We also develop transformations for weakly singular integrands. Placing the scaling center at a point singularity exposes the radial power cancelled by the Jacobian, while generalized radial scalings and Gauss--Jacobi quadrature handle fractional powers. A transverse scaled-boundary map provides the analogous construction for affine singular sets, with straight-line examples in three dimensions. Numerical examples verify polynomial exactness on affine polyhedra and a four-dimensional tesseract, rapid convergence on curved B-spline and NURBS solids, and the expected convergence improvements for point and line singularities. Near-boundary singularity tests also identify when additional patch subdivision or patch-parameter transformations are required.
item.dc:creator: Eric B. Chin, N. Sukumar

item.title: Shape calculus and automatic differentiation for multi-phase level-set topology optimisation with unfitted finite elements
item.description: arXiv:2609.15084v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present shape calculus techniques and a scalable automatic shape differentiation framework for multi-phase topology optimisation on unfitted discretisations defined by several level-set functions. First we establish general, exact shape calculus expressions in the discrete case for multi-phase systems by leveraging concepts from convex geometry. To complement this theoretical foundation, we introduce an open-source multi-phase automatic shape differentiation framework based on polytopal cutting. This computational framework is validated against both finite differences and our established exact expressions, matching the latter to near machine precision. Furthermore, the proposed automatic shape differentiation is scalable across distributed computing environments, demonstrating near ideal weak scaling up to 1.65 billion finite elements across 13,824 computer cores. We demonstrate our implementation by solving unfitted multi-phase topology optimisation problems for anisotropic diffusion, linear elasticity, and fluid--structure interaction. Together, these theoretical and computational contributions provide a robust and accessible foundation for advancing multi-phase topology optimisation using unfitted finite element methods. In particular, the methods enable the solution of topology optimisation problems involving multi-phase and multi-physics systems with non-trivial boundary conditions. The open-source software is available at https://github.com/zjwegert/GridapTopOpt.jl.
item.dc:creator: Zachary J. Wegert, Martin Berggren, Vivien J. Challis

item.title: Kernel-based collocation methods for Heath-Jarrow-Morton models with Musiela parametrization
item.description: arXiv:1809.05643v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study kernel-based collocation methods for numerical solutions of Heath-Jarrow-Morton models in Musiela parametrization. The methods are Euler-Maruyama approximations of finite-dimensional stochastic differential equations and can be used with standard Monte Carlo procedures for derivative pricing. We give a conditional mean-square error estimate under explicit stability assumptions on the differentiated cardinal basis over the full evaluation region required by the volatility functional. The estimate uses the spatial-radius exponent dictated by the squared-error calculation. Two finite-resolution examples illustrate the method for a Vasicek model and for caplet pricing.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Kinoshita, Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: Finite-Dimensional Type I von Neumann Algebras in PyTorch: A GPU-Accelerated Framework for Random Block-Diagonal Operators
item.description: arXiv:2606.15882v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: torch_vn_algebra is a PyTorch library for numerical work with finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras, i.e. direct sums of matrix algebras. These algebras are central to operator algebra theory and, via commutants of symmetries, describe quantum systems with conserved charges or superselection rules. To our knowledge, no numerical software treats them as a data type with their centre, family of traces, conditional expectations, inclusions and functional calculus. The library fills the gap between computer algebra (exact but small-scale) and quantum simulators (large-scale but limited to Hilbert-space matrices): it handles batches of operators on CPUs and GPUs with automatic differentiation, and converts operators, states and channels. Key features: Compact tensor representation: 4D tensor (B, C, kmax, kmax), where B is batch size (e.g. Monte Carlo samples), C is the number of summands, and kmax is the max block size, enabling batched GPU processing. Lazy evaluation: matrix data materialized only on access, avoiding memory waste. Random operator generation: custom eigenvalue distributions; Haar, SU(n), COE, CSE unitary ensembles. Functional calculus and spectral methods: matrix absolute value, square root, inverse, entropy via SVD; automatic switch between exact diagonalization (block size up to 256) and power iteration for extreme eigenvalues. Three trace functionals: Tr_blunt (sum of block traces), Tr_norm (dimension-normalized), tau_vN (faithful normal tracial state). Performance: on a Tesla P100 GPU, processing 20,000 samples of 100x100 operators yields up to 30x speedup over traditional CPU workflows. Availability: open-source at https://gitlab.com/a.hobukob/von_neumann_type_i/
item.dc:creator: Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov

item.title: Sign Propagation of Principal Minors in Fully Semimonotone Matrices and Stone's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.22829v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stone conjectured in 1981 that every fully semimonotone $\mathbf{Q}_0$-matrix is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix; Murthy and Parthasarathy (1995) proved this for orders up to $4$ and for several special classes. We study the principal minors of fully semimonotone matrices $A\in\Ezerof$ without using $\Qzero$. Let $\G(A)$ be the graph whose vertices are the index sets $\alpha$ with $\det A_{\alpha\alpha}\neq 0$ (including $\alpha=\emptyset$), two vertices being adjacent when they differ in exactly one index. We prove that the sign of the principal minor is constant on every connected component of $\G(A)$, and positive on the component of $\emptyset$. Consequences: an $\Ezerof$-matrix with no vanishing principal minor is a $\mathbf{P}$-matrix, and any $\Ezerof$-matrix satisfying a simple ``descending'' condition on its nonvanishing minors is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix. We show that a sign change across two steps through vanishing minors forces strictly positive coupling in the corresponding principal pivotal transform, and that a principal submatrix of minimal order with negative determinant is an almost-$\mathbf{P}_0$ matrix whose inverse lies in $\Ezerof\cap\Nzero$ and has zero diagonal. Explicit examples show that the component structure can contain negative components, that $\det A>0$ does not force $A\in\Pzero$ in $\Ezerof$, that $\Ezerof$ is not invariant under $A\mapsto A+\varepsilon I$, and that $\Ezerof\cap\Pzero$ contains matrices with $\det A>0$ outside $\Qzero$. Stone's conjecture itself remains open.
item.dc:creator: Sajal Ghosh

item.title: Computing Lewis Weights to High Precision by Fixed-Point Iteration
item.description: arXiv:2609.04338v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\ell_p$-Lewis weights of a matrix are defined by a fixed-point equation. For $p<4$, Cohen and Peng [CP15] showed that iterating an equivalent rearrangement of this equation computes Lewis weights to high precision; for $p\geq4$, prior high-precision methods instead use optimization-based approaches. We show that the direct Lewis fixed-point iteration, appearing in the thesis of Lee [Lee16], computes Lewis weights to high precision for every $p>2$. For a matrix $\mathbf{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ partitioned into row blocks $\mathbf{A}_{[1]},\ldots,\mathbf{A}_{[k]}$, we compute, for $p>2$, coordinatewise $\varepsilon$-approximate $\ell_p$ block Lewis weights in $O\left(p\log\frac{p\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^k\operatorname{rank}(\mathbf{A}_{[i]})}}{\varepsilon}\right)$ rounds of exact leverage-score-vector computations. For ordinary Lewis weights, this becomes $O\left(p\log\frac{p\sqrt{m}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, improving the $O\left(p^2\log(m/\varepsilon)\right)$ bound of Gribling, Sidford, and Zhang [GSZ26] for $p\geq4$. Our guarantees also extend to approximate leverage-score computations. Our main observation is that each direct Lewis update contracts the KL divergence to the true weights by a factor of $1-\frac{2}{p}$. We also give an alternate explanation of this contraction through volume sampling and entropic independence. Synthetic experiments closely match our predicted local contraction rates and iteration counts grow approximately linearly with $p$; real-data experiments illustrate the information-concentration tradeoff of finite-$p$ block Lewis designs.
item.dc:creator: Swati Padmanabhan

item.title: AURA: Angular Update Rate Adaptation for training complex-valued neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.25914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs) are increasingly adopted for complex-valued data; however, they are often trained with first-order optimizers inherited from the real-valued case. The efficiency of these methods depends largely on the step size, and their step-size rules ignore the angular information available in the complex plane. We address step-size adaptation in the complex domain by introducing AURA (Angular Update Rate Adaptation), a per-parameter step-size adaptation that can be added on top of any first-order optimizer, and removed from it, without altering its update direction. AURA measures the agreement between consecutive updates of each complex parameter, in length, alignment, and sense of rotation, and enlarges the step when they are consistent and reduces it when they are not. It requires no additional gradient evaluations and only inexpensive vector operations per step. We combine AURA with Adam and Muon and compare the resulting methods with well-known first-order optimizers on four test cases of increasing complexity, ranging from the approximation of scalar complex functions to physics-informed training. Fully connected neural networks are used throughout this work. All hyperparameters other than the step size are held fixed across test cases; for one case, we also tune the hyperparameters of each optimizer under the same budget. Our empirical tests show that AURA improves the convergence of its base optimizer in most cases with a small per-step overhead, and we identify the conditions under which it fails to do so.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Ballini, Allan Peter Engsig-Karup, Tito Andriollo
